rationales.A: Background from the books: the act repealed that line instead of keeping it; the passage leaves the choice to the settlers.
rationales.B: The act refuses to legislate slavery in or out and leaves the people “perfectly free” to form their own institutions — the vote, not Congress, decides.
rationales.C: The passage says the act would not legislate slavery into any territory; it protects no side, it leaves the choice open.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the act declared the Missouri Compromise line inoperative and void; the passage does not keep the line.
rationales.general:
1. Read what the act refuses to do: it will not legislate slavery in, and it will not exclude it.
2. Read what it does instead: it leaves the people “perfectly free” to form their own institutions.
3. Name the idea: that is popular sovereignty, the settlers voting on slavery for themselves.
Remember: when a law says “perfectly free,” ask who gets to choose.
